item.research_question: Can a high-entropy perovskite oxide be used as a highly active and durable air electrode for reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells?
item.processing_route: Sol-gel method with a 2:1:1 mol ratio for citric acid/total metal ions/EDTA, pH value adjusted to ~ 7, and calcined at 1000 °C for 5 h
item.test_conditions: 600 °C, 100 mL min−1 air flow, 80 mL min−1 dry hydrogen gas flow, 5% H2O-Ar atmosphere
key_findings: Peak power density of 1.21 W cm−2 in fuel cell operation
Current density of − 1.95 A cm−2 in electrolysis operation at 1.3 V
Improved electrochemical performance and durability due to high electrons/ions conductivity and hydration reactivity
Low polarization resistance (Rp) of 0.01 Ω cm2 at 700 °C
High oxygen-ion conductivity of 0.064 S cm−1 at 750 °C
item.mechanism: The high-entropy perovskite oxide PLNBSCC exhibits excellent triple conductivity and hydration reactivity due to the promotion of overall conductivity and hydration by various trivalent rare earth elements and divalent alkaline earth metal elements at the A-site
item.future_work: Developing advanced high-entropy structured R-PCEC electrodes
quotes: High-entropy perovskite oxide can be anticipated to accelerate reaction rates in both fuel cell and electrolysis modes

The significantly enhanced electrochemical performance and durability of the PLNBSCC air electrode is attributed mainly to the high electrons/ions conductivity, fast hydration reactivity and high configurational entropy

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a high-entropy perovskite oxide be used as a highly active and durable air electrode for reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells?. System: Pr1/6La1/6Nd1/6Ba1/6Sr1/6Ca1/6CoO3−δ (PLNBSCC). Processing: Sol-gel method with a 2:1:1 mol ratio for citric acid/total metal ions/EDTA, pH value adjusted to ~ 7, and calcined at 1000 °C for 5 h. Test conditions: 600 °C, 100 mL min−1 air flow, 80 mL min−1 dry hydrogen gas flow, 5% H2O-Ar atmosphere. Findings: Peak power density of 1.21 W cm−2 in fuel cell operation; Current density of − 1.95 A cm−2 in electrolysis operation at 1.3 V; Improved electrochemical performance and durability due to high electrons/ions conductivity and hydration reactivity; Low polarization resistance (Rp) of 0.01 Ω cm2 at 700 °C; High oxygen-ion conductivity of 0.064 S cm−1 at 750 °C. Mechanism: The high-entropy perovskite oxide PLNBSCC exhibits excellent triple conductivity and hydration reactivity due to the promotion of overall conductivity and hydration by various trivalent rare earth elements and divalent alkaline earth metal elements at the A-site. Future work: Developing advanced high-entropy structured R-PCEC electrodes. Quote: "High-entropy perovskite oxide can be anticipated to accelerate reaction rates in both fuel cell and electrolysis modes"
